To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) no evidence of measles virus or canine distemper antibody reactivity was found in the sera of 20 multiple sclerosis (MS) patients and 20 age‐matched controls with other neurological diseases; 2) competitive binding studies of cerebrospinal (CSF) fluids from 12 MS patients and 12 controls showed no evidence of preferential reactivity of antibodies to measles virus versus canine distemper (CDV) virus antigens in MS patients; 3)
the antibody response to canine distemper and measles viruses is not significantly different in multiple sclerosis patients and control patients.
1) the canine distemper and measles viruses have similar antigenic properties, and 2) the measles virus has a higher affinity for human brain tissue.
